gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the GardePro A3S takes outside power only through a 4.0 × 1.7 mm 12 V plug. GardePro's $18 12V/1A adapter fits only the A3 and A3S, while its other cameras use a 5.5 × 2.1 mm plug. None states either that GardePro supports 512 GB cards in the A3S, where TechGearLab's table says 128 GB max.
standout_why: I compared against Outdoor Life's Best Trail Cameras 2026 and TechGearLab's Best Trail Camera, both cited. Outdoor Life does not cover the A3S at all. It does already say the Tactacam REVEAL Pro 4.0 Solar is 'not compatible with previous lithium cartridge models' and gives its 'DC 12V-2A' input, so I did not count those as new. TechGearLab lists the A3S as 'SD (128GB max)' and 'AA Batteries (8)'. It does not mention external power, plug sizes or solar for any camera, so the A3S plug, adapter and solar-panel details are not on either page, and its card limit conflicts with GardePro's. TechGearLab covers the original Spypoint Flex-M, not the FLEX-M2, so nothing there describes the FLEX-M2 Solar Bundle or what comes in it. The Wirecutter page (through the proxy) returned 403, so I could not check it.
decides: This confirms the A3S as the budget non-cellular pick and adds what buyers need to run it longer than AA cells last. Use GardePro's A3/A3S adapter (4.0 × 1.7 mm, 12 V/1 A) or the SP350 solar panel set to 12 V on the 4.0 × 1.7 mm plug. Do not use the 5.5 × 2.1 mm adapter sold for GardePro's E- and X-series cameras. A 512 GB card is within GardePro's own A3S limit. For the budget cellular slot, the FLEX-M2 Solar Bundle at $129.99 includes the 5 W solar panel, so buyers don't need to work out solar compatibility separately. None of this changes the order of ChatGPT's picks.
